t.E262.agn: JECFA has noted that acetic acid from vinegar is regularly consumed by humans. In 1973 JECFA set the group ADI for acetic acid and its potassium/sodium salts as 'not limited', and this decision was maintained in 1997. For sodium diacetate, JECFA also set a separate ADI of 0–15 mg/kg body weight in 1973, stating that it is expected to be metabolised like other acetate salts.
t.E262.body: Acetate is a compound involved in the body's normal metabolism.
t.E262.eval: The sodium salt of acetic acid (the acid in vinegar); acetate is involved in the body's normal metabolism. In 1973 JECFA set the group ADI for acetic acid and its potassium/sodium salts as 'not limited'; the decision was maintained in 1997. A separate ADI of 0–15 mg/kg body weight/day was set for sodium diacetate.
t.E262.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E262.prod: Obtained by neutralising acetic acid with sodium carbonate; acetic acid may be produced by fermentation or chemical synthesis.
t.E262.pw.0: It is a source of sodium. Sodium from additives is usually less than that from salt.
t.E262.regx.1: Group I additive; generally authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E262.summary: The sodium salts of acetic acid. They regulate acidity, give a vinegar taste to crisp seasonings and prevent mould in bakery products.
t.E262.what: It is the sodium salt of acetic acid and is used as a preservative and acidity regulator.
